newsitem.title: GERMANY: Three German public banks plan securities firm.
newsitem.headline: Three German public banks plan securities firm.

text.p: Three German regional banks will soon agree to set up a joint securities settlement company to save costs, the head of one of the banks said on Tuesday.

The three banks -- Suedwestdeutsche Landesbank, Landesbank Hessen-Thueringen (Helaba) and Bayerische Landesbank -- will reach a decision in the next few weeks, Werner Schmidt, the chief executive of SuedwestLB, told a news conference.
The publicly-owned banks are central clearing banks for the savings banks in the southern German states of Hesse, Bavaria, Thuringia and Baden-Wuerttemberg.

The talks come against a backdrop of expected consolidation among German banks which are struggling to cut costs and gain the critical mass needed to survive competition after European monetary union.

The planned bank, to be called Wertpapierbank-Sued, will carry out bourse transactions on behalf of the savings banks and hold customers' securities on deposit for them. It will cater for about two million savings bank customers.
The bank will not trade in securities on its own-account and will not be a fund management firm.
It will have to start work by mid-1998 to be up-and-running in time for the planned launch of European monetary union on January 1, 1999, Schmidt said.
The regional banks are still discussing what data processing system to use for the banks and how the savings banks should adapt their own systems to it.

Seperately, Schmidt also said SuedwestLB had reached cooperation agreements with Italy's Banco Ambrosiano Veneto, Austria's Erste Oesterreichische Sparcasse-Bank AG as well as with banks in Argentina, Brazil, Chile and Mexico.

SuedwestLB also planned to open representative offices in Budapest, Warsaw and Prague, Schmidt said. The cooperation agreements were aimed at improving services to exporters based in Baden-Wuerttemberg, Schmidt said.
